text: This town is in the United States, but you can't drive there without leaving the United States.
This is Point Roberts, Washington. About thirteen square kilometres, and twelve hundred people.
In eighteen forty-six, Britain and America split this region along a straight line: the forty-ninth parallel.
The line didn't care about the coast. It sliced right through this peninsula, and left its tip on the American side.
So to reach the rest of America by land, you drive about forty kilometres through Canada, and cross the border twice.
Older kids have long taken a school bus through Canada: four border crossings, every school day.
And when the border shut in twenty twenty, the whole town was cut off by land for over a year and a half.
Would you live in an American town where you need a passport to go shopping in America?
